verdict.tagline: A vast galaxy awaits behind brutal startup barriers and steep learning curves.
for_you_if: you want an immersive space simulation in virtual reality
you can absorb a heavy grind for progression
you have the patience to master complex systems
not_for_you_if: you will not link a separate third-party account
you expect a functional tutorial on your first launch
you need stable performance without startup crashes

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the user interface relies on multiple button clicks, has walls of text, features no search function for keybindings, and uses a clunky wheel menu on foot.

citations.review_text: Gave up in the tutorial. Very clunky UI. At the point I gave up, I was trying to find a "regulator" in a dark room and the light was about a bright as a glow worm. Pressing the "L" key gave a brief light before the glow worm tired itself out.  Did they learn nothing from DOOM 3?? Waste of my time and money.

I say no due to this game being the most not new player friendly game i have ever played. the learning curve is horrible. objectives only briefly explained in the info thing on your hub. walls of text to read through to do some of the most trivial of tasks. and navigation being one of the most aggravating things to get use to. managed to get a good hang of it before running into the next hurdle. 

game is fun once you get a hang of each system but definitely takes patience and a lot of time. not so much a marathon more of an extensive walk to another country.  

(if there is a group with some level of patience that wouldn't mind helping with some of these systems it would be much appreciated.)

One of those games I wish I could give a mediocre rating. Flying around in your spaceship is really cool. Great sound design. But the game is literally a universe wide and an inch deep. Missions (at least in my 15 hours) consist of flying to this place, pick up something or kill something, then flying to another place and turn the mission in. That's the game. From what I can tell, the game is all grind to work towards goals that let you grind a little bit faster. There's no story, no feeling that I'm really doing anything to influence the universe. 

My biggest complaint is the UI is absolutely atrocious. Everything is behind multiple button clicks for zero reason. People say that you get used to it. It's hard to get used to having to do 8 button presses just to turn in a mission. And for a game with hundreds of keybind options, there is no search function. Absolutely mindboggling.

so i really try to like the game, but this wheel menu on foot must be a bad joke. you can't seriously tell me, that this can go through QA and nobody says anything?
my girlfriend literally just refunded the game, because it's impossible for her to choose any item from the wheel in the tutorial (first impressions matter you know?)
The steering is unintuitive, the navigation slow. The idea of the ingame ui sounds nice but is horrible.

citations.review_text: Probably the most unfriendly to beginners game I've ever seen. Tutorial is terrible and doesn't really teach you what you need to know for actually surviving as well as thriving. Youre going to forget all of the things it taught you the second time you log into the game and you will be absolutely lost. Doesnt teach you how the mining works, how to build your ship, doesnt teach you how to scan things or where to buy the scanner. Its like someone gives you all the parts to build a rocket and no instructions and you only have 3 hours. so far ive blown up, sat in a queue trying to leave the hangar and got fined even tho i have no idea why they wont move or why im in an auto leave from the hangar and it puts me in a 10 minute queue to both enter and leave the station. Doesnt teach you how to fill your ship with gas either btw. They literally are like heres a ship, heres your guy and good ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ luck. If this game had an actual story and tutorials that make it feel like your going somehwere and has some guidance it would really halp the flow of the game. You should be able to completely not follow the story if you don't want to but you should still have a better opening to your game that actually helps new players understand all your systems. it feels confusing, convoluted, and pointless for the most part cause your either confused or dead the entire time and your just sitting in an empty expanse with no players to talk to just youtubing how the ♥♥♥♥ to play the game your 20 hours into and still have 0 idea how to gather resources, fight, or do anything to have fun. Just seems empty and lifeless with allot to do and no idea how to do it.
The game literally tells you nothing on how to play except a short tutorial,and i dont really enjoy scouring forums and multiple 3rd party sites to learn about a game.

i had a awful time. i couldnt figure anything out i spent 4 of the 5 hours watching videos on how to play and the rest was looking in circles to find my marker then over shooting my destination 74 times. the frustration was unreal lol 

why cant you add a side indicator for a marked target? the hyperdive assist or whatever was nice but it went away and i have no idea why because nothing is explained. i may try this game again later but right now im taking a break for my monitors sake.

VERY hard game. That alone isn't a problem, but the real issue is it lacks a strong tutorial, and the tutorial it has explains very basic stuff, then completely ignores like 80% of the remaining mechanics. Even with a friend's constant on-call help, I [i[still[/i] can't get anything done! I'm just stuck beyond help, and can't learn.

I adore Elite, but its not an easy game to just jump into. Be warned this game can be a serious time suck. You need to invest in it to get solid enjoyment out of it. 

Once you get past the initial training its learning curve is steep. Getting to grips with the menus, space flight and dated system mechanics can be daunting, but even with all of that I just love the game. Its the friction that drives you to want to keep playing. So Yes I would recommend this game, but it isnt for everyone.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the keybind configuration interface lacks a search feature and has a confusing naming scheme.

citations.review_text:
TLDR: 
Immersive space game with questionable ux and gameplay decisions. Could be better if the devs had brains instead of styrofoam in their heads. 


Great sound and immersive interface design and enjoyable ship piloting. Real scale galaxy with billions of star systems, unexplored or filled with player made infrastructure and semi-organic economy, 

The visuals of planets, stars and other objects could be more diversified though. Real universe may be unfathomably big and boring but I don't think few more picturesque looking black holes, neutron stars and brown dwarfs would hurt.

On the other side game has an enormous set of adjustable key binds, with confusing naming scheme, important binds unassigned by default and NO SEARCH FEATURE. Every time I return to this game I have to relearn the controls from scratch.

The game has a problem with providing information. About anything. Tutorial is very bare bones, if you want to learn more than just basic ship controls you'll find yourself scouring through the discord, reddit posts and youtube videos. Best ship modules are gated behind features like guardian tech and engineering, but you won't know how to interact with them without spending hours looking for information or a lot of frustrating trial and error. 

Finding cargo, systems with ores you want to mine, ships you want to buy, upgrades you want to install requires you to find them yourself or CLOSE THE GAME and LOOK IT UP ON EXTERNAL WEBSITE- why is that not integrated into the game?

There is a large variety of activities but there appears to be a clear meta of most profitable ones, which comes down to buying the largest ship and playing mind-numbing space trucking simulator. There is a colonization system - you can build outposts, stations and Industries. But creating them is based on - of course - trucking cargo to construction sites. The only point of colonization is to engage with the economy and leave a permanent legacy in the galaxy, which may be attractiv…

Great idea, nice flying, beautiful visuals and sound, but I fear it's not playable.

Co-op desyncs randomly, multiple times a day. After disengaging superdrive with a friend, 2 out of 3 times the game just turns black on one of our PCs. And as if that's not enough, there are random crashes with various error codes during gameplay.

So half of your evening is spent trying to get a synced session up and running, only for it to crash after a while. Hideous.

Ah, and the keybind configuration UI sucks.

TLDR: 
Immersive space game with questionable ux and gameplay decisions. Could be better if the devs had brains instead of styrofoam in their heads. 


Great sound and immersive interface design and enjoyable ship piloting. Real scale galaxy with billions of star systems, unexplored or filled with player made infrastructure and semi-organic economy, 

The visuals of planets, stars and other objects could be more diversified though. Real universe may be unfathomably big and boring but I don't think few more picturesque looking black holes, neutron stars and brown dwarfs would hurt.

On the other side game has an enormous set of adjustable key binds, with confusing naming scheme, important binds unassigned by default and NO SEARCH FEATURE. Every time I return to this game I have to relearn the controls from scratch.

The game has a problem with providing information. About anything. Tutorial is very bare bones, if you want to learn more than just basic ship controls you'll find yourself scouring through the discord, reddit posts and youtube videos. Best ship modules are gated behind features like guardian tech and engineering, but you won't know how to interact with them without spending hours looking for information or a lot of frustrating trial and error. 

Finding cargo, systems with ores you want to mine, ships you want to buy, upgrades you want to install requires you to find them yourself or CLOSE THE GAME and LOOK IT UP ON EXTERNAL WEBSITE- why is that not integrated into the game?

There is a large variety of activities but there appears to be a clear meta of most profitable ones, which comes down to buying the largest ship and playing mind-numbing space trucking simulator. There is a colonization system - you can build outposts, stations and Industries. But creating them is based on - of course - trucking cargo to construction sites. The only point of colonization is to engage with the economy and leave a permanent legacy in the galaxy, which may be attractiv…

Title: 81 hours in and I finally get it

Rating: Recommended

Hours Played: 81.0 hrs

I am 54 years old. I have been playing video games since the late 70s. I have seen every space game come and go, from Elite on the BBC Micro to Star Citizen's never-ending crowdfunding campaign. So when I say this game surprised me, I mean it.

I bought Elite Dangerous on a sale with low expectations. I thought it would be pretty but shallow. And for the first 10 hours, I wasn't sure. The learning curve is a wall. The tutorials are basic. The game throws you into a Sidewinder and basically says "good luck." But I stuck with it because something felt right. The way the ship moved. The hum of the reactor. The sheer silence when you cut throttle in deep space.

Now at 81 hours, I am hooked. Not in a frantic, addicted way. In a slow, comfortable way. Like learning to sail or flying a small plane. You get better because you have to. The game does not hold your hand and that is a relief at my age. I am tired of waypoints and quest markers and NPCs telling me I am the chosen one. Here, you are nobody. Just a pilot with a loaned ship and a galaxy to figure out.

Let me break down why this works for me.

The sound design is the best I have ever heard. And I have heard a lot. The frame shift drive charging up never gets old. The way your canopy cracks when you get too close to a star. The computer voice telling you about a planetary scan. It all feels physical. Like you are inside a machine that has weight and risk. Play with good headphones. Do not skip this.

The scale is not a gimmick. It is a tool. When you fly 200,000 light seconds to a station, that is not a loading screen. That is you committing to the trip. You check your phone. You make a cup of tea. You watch the star get bigger and bigger until it fills your whole screen. It forces you to slow down. At my age, I appreciate that more than I expected.

claims.claim: Reviewers report encountering random application crashes, black screens upon exiting supercruise, and connection desynchronization during cooperative play.

citations.review_text:
Great idea, nice flying, beautiful visuals and sound, but I fear it's not playable.

Co-op desyncs randomly, multiple times a day. After disengaging superdrive with a friend, 2 out of 3 times the game just turns black on one of our PCs. And as if that's not enough, there are random crashes with various error codes during gameplay.

So half of your evening is spent trying to get a synced session up and running, only for it to crash after a while. Hideous.

Ah, and the keybind configuration UI sucks.

My experience for the last 3 hours:

- Log in the game, disembark to a station to buy gear to do operations, games crashes and I get stuck on a black screen.

- Join an operation, board a ship and kill waves of stupid enemies that takes 2 full magazines each to kill, cannot finish objective because the last enemies are stuck somewhere bugged and we cannot find them. The mission fails and it tries to restart us at checkpoint. The game crashes.

- Fed up with bugged operations, I decide to do a trade run I buy goods and dock to a station to sell them, my ship clips the dock entrance and gets stuck unable to move, a timer starts and my ship gets blown up by police for "loitering", I lose my ship and my cargo. I get sent to prison 1 hour away from my location.

- Frustrated with that experience I go clean my house and have 20x times more fun (and I hate cleaning my house)

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as having a very steep learning curve for beginners.

citations.review_text: Large learning curve but great flight model.  This is a very Immersive space simulation, especially in VR.

Very cosy spaceflight sim, with a pretty awesome community. The game is kind of hard to get into, it took me a few tries, so I can only recommend this if you are patient enough to struggle through the basics. Also, using a HOTAS is highly recommended if you for some reason have one laying around.
STEEEEEEEEEEP learning curve. Fun once you get the hang of it.
Massive learning curve. Good fun once you get through the start. What other games let you wander off into the unknown for years at a time? The community is great too.

This game has a VERY STEEP learning curve. There are menus it doesnt mention until you need them to scan things, FA off mode that really should automatically enable relative mouse controls, and a BGS system that after 2000 hours I have just begun to understand how to use it to my benefit instead of just randomly yelling a faction's name before roasting another Elite eagle in a Conflict Zone.

THAT BEING SAID, I have never been more awestruck at the things I've seen in this game and from this community. Be it deep space pictures, breaking open asteroids, the explosion of a Thargoid Titan, or the massive payouts of wing expansion missions and the Booze cruise there is something for everyone to do in this game. The credit grind has never been this easy to get through, and the engineering changes recently have made it very possible to actually see progression even when you can only play on weekends and have an actual job. Squadrons are a great tool to group with friends, share resources, or find an online community of CMDRS that can help you out if you're new.

This game is a SPACE SIM more than any other part. You will have to fly places (sometimes very far away) to shoot up bad guys (or good guys), collect materials, engineer modules one by one, build out your spaceship for what you want piece by piece, and if you are playing in Open deal with Gankers and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ BUT also the pilots of the AXI and Fuel Rats. Just like any other game the people are the best and worst part about playing in an open galaxy, but a group of friends in a wing going after Spec ops, raiding settlement, or blowin up bugs never gets old.

Solo this game can be a massive undertaking to get to the "end game" as it were where you have ALL the money, materials, and credits you need. I did it, a few friends of mine did too way back when, but I have to recommend playing this with friends. You can do everything in solo play, a private group, or open regardless; but I have to say colonizing syste…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game requires relying on third-party websites, tools, and external guides to understand its mechanics and find information.

citations.review_text:
TLDR: The game has a lot of potential for fun if you want to explore, get into spaceship fights, or truck millions of tons of goods through space, but many aspects of the game are either lacking in depth or extremely difficult to learn without guides and extensive research, and all of it is extremely grindy, often to a frustrating degree.
TLDR over, more ranty details below.
-----
There's a lot to like about this game, but there's also just a massive amount of padding that makes.. achieving most things in the game feel extremely tedious. 

If you don't really care about min-maxing and just wanna wander around in a huge sandbox, it's pretty interesting to poke at planets and explore the galaxy, and the game's visuals and sense of scale can be awe-inspiring even despite its age. You really feel the scale of the galaxy with how long it takes to do things, which is... not a good thing for anything besides exploration and roleplaying as a deep-space scientist and trailblazer. (Those are fun, though admittedly shallow gameplay loops.)

However doing basically anything beyond that usually requires knowledge that the game doesn't provide reasonable ways to discover. You are either reading guides, wiki-diving, and installing a half-dozen add-ons, or you will spend days to weeks figuring out relatively basic things.

Rewards for most content in the game are pitiful, and upgrading and redesigning your loadouts for ships and personal gear is satisfying but EXTREMELY time-consuming, even with optimal strategies. Many ships in the game don't serve a purpose once you compare their stats to others in the same category, and many gameplay loops also serve no purpose once you realize how poor their rewards are for the time spent on them. This is doubly true for many older ships or gameplay loops that have been obsoleted, but not had their acquisition requirements reduced.

Many elements of the game that aren't just, the flight model and space combat are extremely underdeveloped, or wh…

I love this game.... I want to love it so much... and parts of it I do. But... it's also one of the most frustrating gaming experiences I've ever had. [spoiler][i]And I played Rust guys.[/i][/spoiler]

1. If the other comments make you think it's a bit grindy... think [b]100x of what you thought.[/b]

2. [b]Horrible optimization.[/b] In stations, sometimes you get a semi-permanent FPS reduction from a stable 60 to 10 (YES, TEN) until you quit to menu and go back in. This happens about once every 2 hours.

3. The [b]worst anti-aliasing you've ever seen[/b] in a game. I'm fairly convinced none of them actually do anything, and the game seems to render at a lower-than-native resolution too.

4. [b]The game is pay to win.[/b] Don't listen to anyone telling you it isn't. If you're planning to play online (not solo), you will be ganked and instantly blown to pieces. Which is why barely anyone plays online now. It's only griefers and whales out there now...

5. The in-game UI, galaxy map, and generally information when you're trying to find anything is completely and utterly useless. Prepare to use third party tools, [b]another 2 monitors worth of third party tools[/b] in fact. And even then, the bugs of the UI itself will frustrate you to no end. Like setting a target for your jump or targeting a settlement on the planet, which sometimes work, sometimes don't, other times they actually worked but the UI doesn't update, etc.

6. The on foot section of the game (Odyssey DLC) almost made me rage quit and uninstall 3 times in the last 2 days. In short:
  - Even more unoptimized than stations from inside your ship, you can go [b]as low as 5 FPS![/b] In the middle of combat or just getting close to a settlement...
  - When you inevitably need to quit to menu or just head back to the nearest station to resupply, all your settlement [b]raiding progress is reset[/b], so you start over from 0.
  - [b]Completely unbalanced.[/b] You can't actually comfortably start this content. It'l…

Overall it is an amazing space sim, but the grind is real. If you want to experience space and ground combat, mining, trading, exploration and more, this is the game to get. At a 1:1 "replica" of the milky way you will never run out of things to find or do. 

The downsides: The grind, and no VR for on-foot is a bit of a let down. Also the need for third party tools since there is an abundance of info and things to search for. The immense time it takes to master the game as well. The LY jump capability is quite limited where some journeys can take forever (E.G. getting to Colonia).

I left Elite Dangerous about eight years ago because of engineering. What should have been an optional progression system became a mandatory grind that turned ship building into a second job instead of something fun. I recently decided to give the game another chance, hoping years of updates had addressed those problems.

Instead, I found that nearly everything about the game feels like trying to run a footrace underwater.

Engineering is still effectively mandatory if you want to participate in combat without being hopelessly outclassed. The catch? To get the materials needed for engineering, you're often pushed into fighting enemies who are already engineered while you have none of the upgrades yourself. It's a ridiculous progression loop that punishes you for not already having what you're trying to unlock.

Then there's the travel. Want to engineer your weapons? Fly several hundred light-years to one engineer. Need shields next? Fly several hundred more to another NPC. Thrusters? Repeat the process. Instead of playing the game, you're spending hours staring at a jump counter.

Nothing respects your time.

The information overload doesn't help. Every system seems buried beneath multiple layers of menus, submenus, and obscure interfaces. Even after completing the tutorials, the game barely explains its mechanics. You're left searching through third-party websites, YouTube videos, and community spreadsheets just to understand systems that should be explained in-game.

Preparation has become the game.

You spend more time gathering materials, flying across the galaxy, unlocking engineers, pinning blueprints, hunting down obscure resources, and configuring modules than actually doing the activities you logged in to enjoy. Whether it's combat, exploration, or bounty hunting, the setup feels ten times longer than the payoff.

And here's the thing: the game isn't difficult.

It's not challenging in the satisfying sense. It's unfair, convoluted, and intentionally time-co…

This game has been around since the 1980s. This version is greatly improved and if you're looking for a space shooter, or strategy game with some colorful player-driven backstory, you've found it. I find myself lost in the missions and encounters, sometimes grinding through mining missions on space rocks, Always coming back to push the strategy in power play and expansion. Now with a colonization feature where you can grab your own piece of space for your squadron. Or maybe you want to be a spy or a pirate. You can do that. You can use kbm, joystick and throttle, or console style controller. Make sure you get on Discord or at least the Inara.cz web page and you will find all the info you need to begin and strategize, or just go in and cause trouble if you like. Watch out for gankers. Folks that take advantage of you and your new ship, but that's becoming more rare nowadays as there are anti-ganker squadrons. Or maybe you want to be a ganker for the challenge. Get out there Commanders. Space is your playground! o7 
Commander Xernal of the 9th Legion, out.

I have very mixed feelings about this game. While I do enjoy it, it's a mixed bag of "grinds". Just hop on, grind a bit, and...nothing. I'd say pick it up for 5 bucks on Steam sale as it's something to do here and there while we all wait for the eventual collapse of the gaming industry, and from those ashes hopefully a new golden era.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features support for VR, providing an immersive space simulation experience.

citations.review_text: Thankful for the second life Frontier have given this game, and still one of the best VR experiences you can have to date. Relaxing AF
Large learning curve but great flight model.  This is a very Immersive space simulation, especially in VR.

If you've played Elite Dangerous on console, YOU HAVE NOT PLAYED ELITE DANGEROUS!!!

This is a completely different game on PC and holy smokes is it absolutely incredible. If you REALLY want to experience what it's like to fly inside a spaceship in 1:1 scale with real space, playing this in VR is an absolute game changer!

This game is as chill or as intense as you want it to be (although mostly chill). Space haulin' cargo between stations for profit, bounty hunting space pirates, exploring the LITERAL 400 BILLION SOLAR SYSTEMS IN THIS GAME (99.9% of them remain undiscovered, even with this game being 10+ years old).

Just buy it and get into it. There's so much to learn.
fun and beautiful in VR. love the option to play alone or with a group/public.

A high-risk sci-fi simulation sandbox, best played in VR. The graphics have longevity. The gameplay has something for everyone, from boots-on-the-ground FPS to galactic eploration. And it is unforgiving.  

E:D is not for everyone. It takes patience, perseverence, much learning, and some grinding. Its reward: you get to explore the galaxy in one of the most immersive, adrenalin-inducing experience available in gaming.

Dont know what these recent reviews have issue with, all the ships are easy to buy after a few hours of play, it is a very time consuming game, but that was by design... its a SIM, if thats not what you wanted.. go play NMS... thats the arcade version of this. or this genre may not be for you. 

If you own a VR and dont use it for this game... im not sure why you own it. this games scale and feeling in vr is imo why vr was created...

The 3rd party applications you can have like voice attack and inara type pages make this game a really integrated game i love the modularity.

Great game in 2026, and is still getting regular updates. 10/10

Gameplay: 8/10 (At times it's infuriating, however these are incredibly rare and where the game does good at? It does incredibly well)
Story and Writing: 9/10 (The story is compelling, however the true genius is that you aren't being told the story... You write your own story in the universe Frontier has made. Your actions could one day become legend.)
Visuals: 10/10 (Grand views, majestic vistas, space is inherently beautiful, and the engine renders it in all that glory)
Audio: 9/10 (Rarely the sounds blend oddly, but otherwise the sounds themselves are perfect. Rarely do I need to fumble through panels to understand what that one alarm means, also Archer is the best COVAS)
Performance: 7/10 (There are, unfortunately, many bugs in the system. UI systems that are difficult to navigate, menu layouts that are confusing, and NPC behaviors that can be mildly infuriating. I choose to look past these, but they are hard to ignore.)
Replay Value: You'll either love it, or hate it. Either way? Chances are you'll be back for more, if not for the challenge, than for the love of the game itself.

This is not a game that holds your hand. It does not nestle you into a comfortable blanket. Space is inherently dangerous, and made all the more so by shadow corporations, pirates and those seeking to harm you.

I've been playing this game since the Bridging the Gap days. I've participated in massive Community level things, I've put my name on several star systems and planets. Even colonized a system of my very own. The one thing I can say is? You will be challenged in anything you choose to do, and that's the beauty of it: Freedom. There are no rails here. There is no true 'guidance'. You make your own story, your own journey, your own legend.

However you fly, Commander. Whatever you do? Remember to fly dangerously. o7 Commander.

Its kinda wild that the main criticism people have of this game (besides bugs, and my god theres some nasty bugs here and there) are things that'd make the game worse if they were added or changed.
Def one of the more obnoxious playerbases online presence wise. Though, due to being a to scale milky way, it is quite rare to actually encounter anyone even in open play, thus limiting your exposure is pretty easy. And the folks you randomly meet in space usually are pretty chill anyway.
Anyway all that aside, good game. It holds up just fine to modern titles even a decade of relatively few added features later.
